name: Brindle (MBTPS2)
summary: Brindle 1 (BR1), an X-linked variant in MBTPS2 that alters how the gene's transcript is spliced. A mare with one copy has irregular stripes of altered hair texture, sometimes with visible differences in pigment, running from the back down the sides and over the neck, hindquarters and upper legs; they follow which X chromosome each patch of skin uses. A stallion with the variant, and a mare with two copies, have a sparse mane and tail and no classic stripes. A stallion passes it to every daughter and to no son. It is one validated, inherited form of brindle, not the explanation for every brindle-looking horse. It is rare and known from one Quarter Horse and Paint Horse family; no carrier frequency has been published, so none is given here.

phenotypes.name: Sparse mane and tail
phenotypes.description: No normal copy: a stallion with the variant on his one X, or a mare with it on both. The mane and tail are sparse and the coat has no classic stripes. The evidence for mares with two copies is thinner than for stallions: the family the variant was found in had none.

phenotypes.name: Brindle
phenotypes.description: A mare with one copy. Irregular stripes of altered hair texture, less straight and more unruly than the hair beside them, running from the back down the sides and over the neck, hindquarters and upper legs. Some mares also show stripes of differing pigment. How much shows varies widely between horses and between the summer and winter coat, and can come on any base colour.
